title: Lead Management
summary: Develop comfortable equipment routines and practical lead-handling skills that support safe, relaxed walks through positive reinforcement.

subcategories.title: Comfortable Introductions to Walking Gear
subcategories.goal: Help the dog feel comfortable with a harness, lead and the preparation for walks.
subcategories.steps: Introduce each item in a quiet space. Reward relaxed investigation of the equipment, then build gradually towards brief comfortable wearing and attaching the lead. Practise just a few steps indoors before moving outside. Keep each stage easy enough that the dog can participate willingly.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Avoid chasing the dog with equipment or fastening it while they struggle. Pause if they freeze, retreat or mouth the gear. Check fit and comfort rather than assuming reluctance is disobedience.

subcategories.title: Choosing Comfortable Lead Equipment
subcategories.goal: Choose equipment that supports relaxed walking without pain or intimidation.
subcategories.steps: Review the fit and condition of your walking equipment. Select a secure, comfortable harness and an appropriate fixed-length lead for your setting. Practise attaching and removing the lead calmly, rewarding cooperation. Recheck that the dog can move naturally before beginning short walks.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Equipment supports management but does not teach the skill by itself. Avoid equipment designed to tighten, startle or hurt. Check clips and straps regularly, and ask your trainer for help with individual fit needs.

subcategories.title: Lead Holds and Managing Spare Line
subcategories.goal: Build practical handling skills while keeping the lead secure and comfortable.
subcategories.steps: Practise the demonstrated lead holds without a dog first. Rehearse gathering and releasing spare line smoothly, keeping your hands clear of loops. Then practise in a quiet space with your dog, adjusting length before turns or obstacles and rewarding comfortable connection.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Never wind the lead around your hand or fingers. Use handling to manage slack and maintain safety, not to deliver corrections. Practise with your trainer if balance, strength or sudden pulling makes handling difficult.

subcategories.title: Coordinating Lead, Marker and Rewards
subcategories.goal: Improve handler coordination so rewards can be delivered without tightening the lead.
subcategories.steps: Begin stationary in a quiet location. Arrange the lead and food so you can mark and reward a comfortable check-in without fumbling. Add one or two steps, delivering rewards where you want the dog to walk. Rehearse smooth turns and short stretches before adding distractions.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Keep the lead relaxed and avoid using it to place the dog beside you. Short practice helps both partners. Simplify your setup if handling food and a clicker together becomes awkward; a familiar verbal marker can help.

subcategories.title: First Steps with a Relaxed Lead
subcategories.goal: Teach a puppy or beginner dog that moving with the handler on a loose lead is rewarding.
subcategories.steps: Start indoors or in a secure quiet area. Reward being near you with slack in the lead, then take one step and reward following. Build a few steps at a time and add a release for safe sniffing. If the task becomes difficult, pause and reset at an easier level.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Avoid jerking the lead or dragging the dog into position. Reward frequently while learning and keep sessions brief. Meet exploration and exercise needs as well as practising this skill.
